## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [ ] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

C++ frontend API or graph construction

## Summary

Run the callback on a copy, map the returned plans to their original
indices, and apply the existing `reorder_plans()` helper before selecting
index 0. Failed or invalid callback results leave the original ordering
and selection unchanged.

This extends the synchronized-reordering approach from #1340 to the
legacy callback tuner, preserving its callback signature. The native
`Graph::autotune` path is unchanged.

## Why

`Execution_plan_list::autotune` lets its callback reorder or prune
`execution_plans` without updating the corresponding engine configs,
notes, or filter flags. After tuning, metadata queries can describe
a different plan from the one executed.

## Related issues

<!-- Use "Fixes #123" or "Related to #123" where applicable. -->

## API and compatibility impact

<!-- Note public API, supported GPU/cuDNN/CUDA/Python versions, performance, or backward-compatibility changes. Write "None" if not applicable. -->

None

## Testing

<!-- List exact commands and results. If something was not tested, explain why. -->
- Release C++ build passed.
- GPU tests: 5 cases, 970 assertions passed.
- Regression coverage includes plan identity, filtering, replay,
  serialization, and failed tuning.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved execution-plan autotuning by validating callback results and keeping plan details aligned with the selected ranking.
  * Empty, unknown, null, or duplicate plans returned by a callback now result in a clear failure.
  * When legacy autotuning fails, existing plans and their associated selection and notes remain intact.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

reviews.body:
**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `4ed34ffd62de` against base `dde1f51c7a5b`.

Thank you for your contribution! The legacy callback now commits plan ordering and its associated metadata together, and rejects invalid results without losing the previous selection. I found no actionable correctness issue in this change.

Validation: Release C++ build passed. On an H100, the existing [autotune] suite passed all 4 cases / 625 assertions, covering native and legacy sorting/pruning, filtering, winner replay, serialization, and failure preservation. Two additional tests passed 502 assertions: null, foreign, duplicate, empty, and error-returning callback results preserve executable state and permit a valid retry; consecutive three-cycle permutations and subset pruning preserve metadata by plan identity and forward the callback context. The same additional tests compiled against the base failed both cases (31 failed assertions), reproducing invalid-result acceptance, lost state after callback failure, and mismatched plan metadata.

Limitations: Local execution covered Linux/H100; other GPU architectures, Windows, and older backend versions were not independently exercised.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
